[4800475117] Upstream Reporter: Yaakov Selkowitz
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}The python team handles the rebuild of nearly all of ELN's Python packages in rawhide as part of the upgrade, and when that is merged, it is mostly automated now that we include the next Python in Extras. However, because maturin has an {{eln}} branch due to vendoring of Rust crate dependencies, it is skipped by EBS and therefore those packages that {{BuildRequires: maturin}} \(e.g. python-cryptography) can't be built, and then composes and possibly buildroots break etc.

Theoretically, it would be enough for someone to build maturin in the ELN side tag while the mass rebuild is in progress, and then tag the resulting build into {{eln-updates-candidate}} once the mass rebuild update is filed \(since EBS didn't build it, it won't include it in an update even if it's in the side tag). But that requires human intervention at particular times.

We should figure out a better way of handling maturin sometime before the Python 3.16 migration \(June '27?).
{quote}
Upstream URL: https://github.com/fedora-eln/eln/issues/573

Theoretically, it would be enough for someone to build maturin in the ELN side tag while the mass rebuild is in progress, and then tag the resulting build into {{eln-updates-candidate}} once the mass rebuild update is filed \(since EBS didn't build it, it won't include it in an update even if it's in the side tag). But that requires human intervention at particular times.

We should figure out a better way of handling maturin sometime before the Python 3.16 migration \(June '27?).
{quote}
Upstream URL: https://github.com/fedora-eln/eln/issues/573

* ☒ ntpsec
* ☒ systemd
{quote}

Upstream description: {quote}Both chrony and ntpsec use {{ID}} in {{/etc/os-release}} to derive the ["vendor zone"|https://www.ntppool.org/vendors.html] which is configured in these packages. This needs to align to a registered vendor, namely fedora, rather than eln.

Both specs allow the {{vendorzone}} macro to be predefined, so perhaps setting it in the koji build tag will suffice, although perhaps mock configs should also be updated if we go that route.
{quote}
Upstream URL: https://github.com/fedora-eln/eln/issues/567
This work item links to "Upstream issue (Web Link)"

[4635417574] Upstream Reporter: Yaakov Selkowitz
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}protobuf 6 has added a dependency on abseil-cpp, which has then carried into mysql8.4 and usbguard. While it looks like protobuf could support a bundled version, it also seems that it would need to install it anyway as the API is transitive, and it is not header-only, so simply using a system version would be preferred. Unless I'm missing something, that means it will need to come into RHEL 11 as a result.

If so, then {{webrtc-audio-processing}} can also use it directly and drop the bundling for RHEL \(since it was previously the only consumer).

Status: [https://tiny.distro.builders/view-rpm--view-eln--abseil-cpp.html]

/cc @xsuchy
{quote}

[4526736298] Upstream Reporter: Yaakov Selkowitz
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}Once the latest ELN changes are in place in image-builder, then it should be possible to switch the ELN pungi-configs from {{kiwibuild}} to {{image-build}} for those images which correspond to RHEL's.

For images which are uploaded to quay.io, it is important that either the subvariant not change, or that the cloud uploader be updated accordingly, in order to keep the uploads flowing.

However, ELN Live images correspond not to RHEL but to CentOS AltImages, which is using kiwi \(albeit not through pungi as part of a compose), therefore those should not be changed here either.
{quote}
Upstream URL: https://github.com/fedora-eln/eln/issues/531

[4415614879] Upstream Reporter: Adam Williamson
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}When doing a default network / DVD install of Fedora-eln-20260510.n.0, there is no network connection on the installed system. This does not happen with a minimal \("Custom") install, or when installing the GNOME live image.

{quote}
Upstream URL: https://github.com/fedora-eln/eln/issues/516

[4361525935] Upstream Reporter: Yaakov Selkowitz
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}It was reported in #490 that the default package set changed from "Custom Operating System" to "Server with GUI". This was an unplanned symptom of the release package change, which threw off anaconda because of how it did OS detection. Fixing that reverted things to how they were.

However, the default in RHEL is actually "Server with GUI", so this uncovered a previously undetected disparity. This happens because anaconda does NOT define a default group except for Fedora variants, which ELN was being so treated. "Server with GUI" refers to the {{graphical-server-environment}} in comps, which RHEL/ELN variants file list in the first position.

[https://github.com/rhinstaller/anaconda/pull/7041], coming in the future anaconda 45.2, will switch this back to "Server with GUI" in line with RHEL. This will require adjustments to OpenQA which tests the default package set.

/cc @AdamWill
{quote}
Upstream URL: https://github.com/fedora-eln/eln/issues/501

[3261104945] Upstream Reporter: Davide Cavalca
Upstream issue status: Closed
Upstream description: {quote}The CentOS Hyperscale SIG maintains an ELN-tracking package set in copr \([eln-main|https://copr.fedorainfracloud.org/coprs/g/centoshyperscale/eln-main/packages/], [eln-facebook|https://copr.fedorainfracloud.org/coprs/g/centoshyperscale/eln-facebook/packages/]). These are meant to be installed and used on ELN, and should track the current ELN, but we don't currently have a way to automatically rebuild them whenever ELN is rebuilt. We can easily implement the copr rebuild part on our end, but we need a way to programmatically check that a new ELN rebuild has been completed so we can key off of it.
{quote}

[4393549786] Upstream Reporter: Yaakov Selkowitz
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}ELN kernel changed to CONFIG_MODULE_SIG_KEY_TYPE_MLDSA_87 from CONFIG_MODULE_SIG_KEY_TYPE_RSA in 7.0 when openssl 4.0 was briefly available. Without openssl 4.0 at build time, the kernel modules fail to load even with PKCS7_WAIVE_AUTHATTRS_REJECTION_FOR_MLDSA, so it needed to be switched back. Once openssl 4.0 is stable, then the config can be switched again.

See also: #503 [https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2464626] [https://gitlab.com/cki-project/kernel-ark/-/merge_requests/4505]
{quote}
Upstream URL: https://github.com/fedora-eln/eln/issues/509

[4386846578] Upstream Reporter: Adam Williamson
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}See [https://openqa.stg.fedoraproject.org/tests/6345521#step/rmdepcheck_aarch64/42] . In ELN, these packages:

* mingw32-openjph
* mingw64-openjph
* mingw32-libopenjph
* mingw64-libopenjph

are not installable on any arch other than x86_64 due to dep issues:

{noformat}
Pre-existing dependency problems in the tested packages themselves:
package: mingw32-libopenjph-0.27.0-1.eln156.noarch from file:///var/tmp/rdcelnrepoau5mmg50/Extras
  mingw32(libstdc++-6.dll)
package: mingw32-openjph-0.27.0-1.eln156.noarch from file:///var/tmp/rdcelnrepoau5mmg50/Extras
  mingw32(libstdc++-6.dll)
package: mingw64-libopenjph-0.27.0-1.eln156.noarch from file:///var/tmp/rdcelnrepoau5mmg50/Extras
  mingw64(libstdc++-6.dll)
package: mingw64-openjph-0.27.0-1.eln156.noarch from file:///var/tmp/rdcelnrepoau5mmg50/Extras
  mingw64(libstdc++-6.dll){noformat}
The dependencies in question are provided by mingw32-libstdc\+\+ and mingw64-libstdc\+\+ . It looks like on x86_64 these are in CRB \(which Extras is allowed to pull from) but on all the other arches they are not.
{quote}
Upstream URL: https://github.com/fedora-eln/eln/issues/507

Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}The Tools team has created a persistent side tag for GCC snapshots in [https://forge.fedoraproject.org/releng/tickets/issues/13120]. We need to devise a way of using this to detect resulting FTBFS in the ELN package set and address them early in order to alleviate the pressure from mass rebuild failures, particularly prior to the branching of a RHEL major \(coming up with GCC17/F46).
{quote}

[4377654026] Upstream Reporter: Yaakov Selkowitz
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}Since Content Resolver is proving to be valuable, ask other teams to provide better metadata ? specifically so we don't have to parse root.log files to get build dependencies, which is fragile as the format is not guaranteed and has changed a few times in the last few years \(e.g. due to the addition of automated buildrequires, and then migrating to dnf5). An idea would be for e.g. mock to output a machine parseable format of total \(direct) buildrequires.
{quote}
Upstream URL: https://github.com/fedora-eln/content-resolver/issues/108

[4366688017] Upstream Reporter: Yaakov Selkowitz
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}This week's issue with kernel module signing is possibly the first serious breakage of the ELN kernel since we started automating ELN kernel builds, which meant they were gated by Rawhide testing. This was important as it prevented broken kernels from reaching composes, which obviously causes instability for consumers.

The downside is that makes it harder to bisect individual issues, as sometimes a week or two may pass before a rawhide kernel is good enough to reach ELN. @jmflinuxtx has requested we go back to simultaneous builds of ELN kernel, which would require gating to be in place to prevent bad builds from reaching composes. OpenQA for ELN has come a long way since then.

@AdamWill, is this possible to do, and what would it take?

\(Incidentally, this would also solve the "problem" of kernel builds resulting in long waits between batches, and since EBS would just exclude kernel again, we wouldn't have to figure out how to split it out into its own parallel batch, although the support needed to enable Hyperscale might solve that too.)
{quote}
Upstream URL: https://github.com/fedora-eln/eln/issues/503

[4359246497] Upstream Reporter: bhoy-troy
Upstream issue status: Open
Upstream description: {quote}h3. {anchor:summary}Summary
The codebase uses multiprocessing extensively in analyzer.py but may not fully comply with Python 3.14's stricter pickling requirements. Instance methods passed to multiprocessing. Process and objects passed between processes must be properly picklable to avoid serialization failures.

h3. {anchor:background}Background
Python 3.14 enforces stricter requirements for object serialization in multiprocessing contexts. Objects passed to multiprocessing.Process, ProcessPoolExecutor, or through multiprocessing Queue must be picklable.

h3. {anchor:possible-issues-in-analyzerpy}Possible issues in analyzer.py:
* Passes instance method self._analyze_env_process to Process
* Passes env_conf, repo, arch objects through queue - must it be picklable?
* Returns env dict through queue - must it be picklable ?

h3. {anchor:references}References
* Python 3.14 Multiprocessing: [https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/multiprocessing.html]
* Pickle Protocol 5: [https://peps.python.org/pep-0574/]
* DNF and multiprocessing: [[https://dnf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html] |https://dnf.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html]
{quote}
